title: Compass and Harbor
premise: In 1917, the coastal town of Harrow Bay is requisitioned as a naval hospital, and with it, the army seizes every record in the harbor office—including Silas Eastwick's private ledger of the dead and disappeared that officers refused to name. Among the entries is the truth about her brother's desertion, a secret that could save or condemn her remaining family when evacuation berths on the last transport ship are allocated. Silas must trade her silence, and her carefully constructed anonymity, for a single berth, choosing between her ailing mother and the nephew she swore to protect. In the end, she surrenders the ledger publicly, exposing the unnamed dead and securing passage for her nephew, while she and her mother remain behind—finding that belonging was never granted by documents, but by the community that refuses to let her be erased.
about_author: Lior Hartwell is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime port records along the English coast. Their fiction is drawn from the marginalia of official documents—the names written in pencil, in grief, in the spaces the record keepers left blank.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unwritten Names
chapters.summary: Silas tends wounded soldiers at the Harrow Bay field station, recording in her private ledger the names officers omit from official reports. Her mother, Maren, presses her to leave town before the rumored requisition. Silas refuses, bound to the harbor, the ledger, and the memory of her brother Edmund. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Army officers arrive and claim the town, the harbor office, and every document within it—including, by clerical error or design, Silas's ledger. Colonel Ashworth, cold and precise, catalogues her brother's desertion file among the seized papers. Silas realizes her secret is now military property. POV: Silas, with a brief interlude from Ashworth's perspective. Emotional beat: violation and the collapse of her invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Silas navigates the occupied town, discovering the ledger's contents are being used to screen families for evacuation priority—and that Edmund's entry marks the Eastwicks as suspect. Her nephew Tobias, fifteen and furious, wants to confront the officers. Silas restrains him, learning which silences still hold. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: protective fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: The transport ship Persephone is announced; only a handful of civilian berths remain for Harrow Bay. Maren's health fails visibly, and Tobias's age makes him eligible for conscription if he stays. Silas petitions the harbormaster, an old friend, and learns the list will be finalized within the week. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the ticking clock made flesh.

chapters.title: Ashworth's Offer
chapters.summary: Colonel Ashworth summons Silas: he will guarantee her a berth and expunge Edmund's record—if she testifies that the ledger's unnamed dead were deserters and criminals, legitimizing the omissions. She recognizes the trap: her silence, once her shield, is now the army's weapon. POV: Silas, with Ashworth's private doubts surfacing. Emotional beat: temptation braided with disgust.

chapters.title: Maren's Truth
chapters.summary: Maren, lucid for the first time in weeks, reveals she has known about the ledger all along—and about Edmund's desertion, which she calls not shame but mercy. She tells Silas to take the berth herself and stop carrying the family alone. Silas, shaken, visits the harbor at night and nearly burns the ledger. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed—not property, but burden and love.

chapters.title: The Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Tobias, defying Silas, breaks into the requisitioned harbor office to steal the ledger back and is caught. Ashworth threatens him with conscription. Silas arrives and, in front of the assembled officers and townsfolk, begins reading the ledger's true names aloud—refusing the bargain. POV: Silas, climaxing into Tobias's stunned witness. Emotional beat: the silence broken; no way back.

chapters.title: Consequence
chapters.summary: Silas is detained; the town, emboldened, petitions en masse for the named dead to be recognized, forcing an inquiry that embarrasses Ashworth's command. Maren deteriorates rapidly. Ashworth, visiting Silas's cell, quietly arranges one berth on the Persephone—no longer a bribe, but an acknowledgment. POV: Silas and Ashworth in alternating scenes. Emotional beat: cost and unexpected grace.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Silas chooses: Tobias sails. At the dock, she gives him the ledger, now his inheritance, and makes him promise to carry the names somewhere they'll be read. Maren, too frail for the journey and at peace with it, stands beside her. The Persephone departs through the mist. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined—the choice made without regret.

chapters.title: Harbor
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Harrow Bay slowly returns to itself; the inquiry restores the names to official record, and the townspeople carve them into the harbor wall. Maren dies in spring, held by Silas and the community that once let her daughter stay invisible. Silas begins a new ledger—not of the omitted, but of the remembered. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: belonging earned, identity claimed, home redefined.
